assumptions: Axisymmetric TE-phi Maxwell model: E_phi, H_r, H_z depend on radius and axial position; azimuthal variation and the other polarization are absent.
The displayed 3D cylinder is a rotational reconstruction of this computed r-z solution, not a general volumetric 3D solver.

Fixed vacuum permittivity and permeability everywhere. The hollow cylindrical shell and bottom are an isotropic Ohmic medium, not an actual metal beverage can or a resolved plasma. The cover closes fraction C of the inner cavity mouth, leaving opening radius (R-wallThickness) sqrt(1-C). Boundary-cell conductivity uses the exact geometric material volume fraction.

J_phi = sigma E_phi; Joule deposition increases a diagnostic temperature using constant density and specific heat. Temperature does not modify conductivity; transport, mechanics, ionization and radiative cooling are absent.
Outer radial and both axial boundaries are PEC; E_phi is regular and vanishes on the axis. No physical escaped-energy term exists for these closed boundaries.
An optional artificial electric damping layer near the outer boundaries is counted separately as sponge loss. It is not a perfectly matched layer and can reflect waves.
The localized impressed azimuthal current has a Gaussian envelope and carrier; its signed work is measured. Source work can be negative when the prescribed source extracts field energy.

Weighted-adjoint cylindrical curls and implicit midpoint are second order in time. Finite-grid spatial error, dispersion and symmetry limitations remain; energy consistency is not experimental validation.
validationScope: Numerical Maxwell/Ohmic consistency and continuum mode convergence; no black-hole, plasma-material, or observational validation.
displayInterpolation: E is sampled at cell centres; H, B and Poynting vectors in fields use adjacent-face arithmetic averages for visualization. Energy uses the raw staggered fields and dual volumes.
heatingDensityBasis: depositedEnergyDensityJPerM3 and joulePowerDensityWPerM3 are per full electric-cell volume; materialFillFraction*rho*cp is the cell heat capacity per full volume. temperatureRiseK retains tiny increments that can round away when added to initialTemperatureK.
